title: A worktree holding only base copies can be removed
why: Incident, Nov 1 22:41 CST, raised at the owner's request by lane merge-lock-record-drift: test-author worktree agent-a7d6329a40cedecfc kept staged copies of four files, each byte for byte equal to the branch base, with no unpushed commit. The shared-tree guard refused its remove and restore; the owner's "override, yes" did not lift it; the stop hook asked to commit and push the stale copies, which would have undone PR #1048.
note: One lane: (1) shared-tree guard: allow worktree remove when every dirty path equals a commit on origin (branch head or base) and no local commit is unpushed; red-first case is this tree. (2) Measured Nov 1 22:42 CST: the bare `override` worked, so "override, yes" failed because the override must be typed alone; accept a reply that starts with the word, or say the override must be typed alone. (3) stop-hook-git-check.sh checks the primary checkout, not the worktree the shell stands in, and skips a tree whose dirty content is all base copies. (4) Cause: test-author and builder briefs take a fresh worktree from the branch head before a fix round. The tree was removed under the owner's bare override, Nov 1 22:42 CST. Ready. Port: yes.
